keyframe_review.note: 5,477 km2 by Cliopatria (4,552 km2 by gazetteer cells; the West Bank admin-1 resolves to 4,805 km2). No page opened gives an area for the West Bank, so no infobox comparison. The shape is the West Bank: right as a place, but the Palestinians were not a state and 'Jordanian forces remained in most positions they held in the West Bank'; the shape is kept as the owner row of the occupation.

correction.text: the same West Bank shape held through 3 April 1949 (armistice) and until the formal annexation on 24 April 1950

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends the Palestinians row in 1948 and gives the West Bank to Jordan from 1949, but the formal annexation was 'on 24 April 1950'. The Jordan dossier's 1949 keyframe removes the West Bank for 1949 to match; from 1950 the land is Jordan's.

region.text: the West Bank, the part of Mandatory Palestine outside Israel that the Arab Legion held

ledger.note: May 1948: the Arab-held West Bank is left to the Palestinians when the Mandate ends. The Palestinians page says only 'Following Israel's declaration of independence in May 1948' five Arab armies intervened and that the areas outside Israel 'were occupied by Egypt or annexed by Jordan'; it describes no Palestinian polity, so the founding is the researcher's bridge to Cliopatria's 1948 shape (the West Bank, about 4,550 km2 by cells).

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: May 1948: the Arab Legion holds the West Bank. 'Areas which did not become part of the newly declared Israeli state were occupied by Egypt or annexed by Jordan' (the Gaza Strip went to Egypt). The Jordan dossier records the mirror event.

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 24 April 1950: the occupation ends in annexation. 'The West Bank was formally annexed on 24 April 1950.'

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 24 April 1950: the West Bank joins Jordan. 'During the December 1948 Jericho Conference' Palestinian notables accepted Jordanian rule and recognised Abdullah I; the Palestinians page: 'At the Jericho Conference on 1 December 1948, 2,000 Palestinian delegates supported a resolution calling for the unification of Palestine and Transjordan'; the annexation followed 'on 24 April 1950', recognised only by the United Kingdom, Iraq and possibly Pakistan.

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 24 April 1950: the Palestinian-held West Bank passes to Jordan. The Gaza Strip, 'partly occupied by Egypt', stays outside it (see the all-palestine-government dossier).

wars.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War

zones.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

wars.outcome: Israel was established; the rest of Mandatory Palestine was 'occupied by Egypt or annexed by Jordan'; hundreds of thousands of Palestinians 'fled or were expelled' and Israel did not let them return.
wars.note: The war's own page is read in the state-of-israel and kingdom-of-jordan dossiers.

certainty.note: The limits of the Arab-held land were the front lines of 1948 until the Jordan armistice of 3 April 1949 (the Green Line, sharp on the western side); the Jordan Valley side is the old Mandate frontier.

sources.title: Palestinians
sources.note: 1947 partition, May 1948, the Jericho Conference (1 December 1948), Egyptian and Jordanian administration. It describes no 1948 Palestinian polity and does not mention the All-Palestine Government in its text.

sources.title: Jordanian annexation of the West Bank
sources.note: Jericho Conference, 3 April 1949 armistice, formal annexation 24 April 1950, recognition.

notes: Written by me-10-j from two pages. WHAT THIS ROW IS: Cliopatria's 'Palestinians' is a single 1948 shape over the West Bank; it is not a state, and neither page opened describes a Palestinian government there. It is kept as the owner of land occupied by Jordan (rule 4 needs an owner), 1948 to the annexation of 24 April 1950, so that the Arab Legion's holding is drawn hatched; this extends the row two years beyond Cliopatria. The founding event is confidence 1. GAZA: the Gaza Strip is not in the shape; it was Egyptian-held, with the All-Palestine Government (22 September 1948 to June 1959, dossier all-palestine-government by me-10-h). The united-arab-republic dossier and the state-of-israel dossier use 'palestinians' as the generic owner of Gaza (1959-1967 and 1967-2005) and the post-1988 West Bank; if the colour agent wants a separate entity for the PLO and the Palestinian National Authority it should seed 'palestinian-national-authority' (named as predecessor in the gaza-hamas dossier) and a 'state-of-palestine' (declared 1988; the Palestinians page gives the proclamation only as '1988') and re-point those events. NOT READ: the 1948 War page for the Palestinian forces, the Arab Higher Committee, the Nakba's land losses; the page budget was two.
